# Environment variables

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-docs.ts from the code (#734 / ADR-237 §2.2). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every environment variable this deployment reads: **101** an operator may set, plus **3** the product sets for itself. The list is walked out of the source, so a variable added tomorrow appears here or the build fails.

A blank value is not the same as a missing one: unless a row says otherwise, unset means the default in the second column, and setting a variable to an empty string means the empty string.

## Runtime

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | development | Set to `production` in any real deployment. It is not cosmetic: below production the API accepts the literal bearer `dev-token`, and the session cookie is not marked `secure`. |
| `SERVER_PORT` | 4000 | Port the API server listens on. |
| `COLLAB_PORT` | 4100 | Port the collaboration (WebSocket) server listens on. |
| `PORT` | 4100 | Port for the operator console process (`operator/main.ts`), which is deployed separately from the API. |
| `WEB_PORT` | 5173 | Port the web dev server listens on. Build output is static, so this affects development only. |
| `WKS_BRAND_NAME` | Wikistead | Product name shown in the interface and in outgoing mail, for a rebranded deployment. |
| `WKS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | unset (links are dropped) | Canonical public base URL (scheme + host, port allowed) for links built off the request path — background mail has no Host header to work from. Unset means a message that needs a link is dropped with a logged reason rather than improvising one. |
| `PUBLIC_TENANT_BASE_HOST` | the request's own Host header | Base host that new workspace subdomains are composed against when signup runs behind a proxy that rewrites Host. |
| `PUBLIC_SHELL_INDEX` | unset (the public HTML shell is off) | Path to the built web `index.html` the server injects public page metadata into. Unset means crawlers and link previews get the SPA's empty shell, so any deployment that publishes pages wants it set. |
| `SITE_HOST` | dev.localhost | The one public host the self-host compose profile answers on. Read by compose and by the Caddy configuration rather than by the application, which learns its host from each request. |

## Database

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | unset (required) | Postgres connection string for the restricted runtime role (no superuser, no BYPASSRLS). This is the credential the API and the collaboration server run every request under. |
| `DATABASE_ADMIN_URL` | falls back to DATABASE_URL | Superuser connection string, used by the migration runner and by the cross-tenant storage sweep. Keep it out of processes that do not need it — row-level security is what confines the runtime role to one workspace. |

## Cache and queues

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VALKEY_URL` | redis://localhost:6379 | Valkey/Redis connection string. Collaboration uses it to fan out between server instances, and rate limits count in it, so all instances must share one. |

## Authorization

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPENFGA_API_URL` | http://localhost:8080 | OpenFGA endpoint. Every permission decision in the product is asked here. |
| `OPENFGA_STORE_ID` | unset (required) | OpenFGA store holding this deployment's tuples. `pnpm dev:up` writes one for development; production creates it once and keeps it. |
| `OPENFGA_MODEL_ID` | unset (the store's latest model) | Pins the authorization model version. Pinning it means a model deployed later cannot silently change how existing tuples are interpreted. |
| `OPENFGA_DATASTORE_ENGINE` | memory | What the OpenFGA service stores tuples in, declared to the API so it can refuse to start on `memory` under production — in-memory tuples vanish on restart, and every permission in the deployment with them. |

## Search

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MEILI_HOST` | http://localhost:7700 | Meilisearch endpoint. |
| `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` | unset | Meilisearch master key. Production refuses to start on the value published in the public repository's fixtures, so generate one. |
| `SEARCH_CURSOR_SECRET` | falls back to GUEST_TOKEN_SECRET | Signs search pagination cursors so a cursor cannot be edited into a query the caller was not authorized for. |

## Object storage

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `S3_ENDPOINT` | the AWS default for the region | S3-compatible endpoint the server itself talks to (MinIO, SeaweedFS, R2, S3). |
| `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` | same as S3_ENDPOINT | The address the BROWSER reaches the store at, when it differs from the one the server uses. A presigned URL's signature covers the Host header, so a URL signed for an internal name is refused the moment a browser opens it under a public one. |
| `S3_REGION` | us-east-1 | Region used when signing. S3-compatible gateways usually ignore it but still expect it to match the signature. |
| `S3_BUCKET` | unset (required) | Bucket that holds attachments, icons and import archives. |
| `S3_ACCESS_KEY` | unset (required) | Access key id for the bucket. |
| `S3_SECRET_KEY` | unset (required) | Secret key for the bucket. |
| `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` | false | Set to `true` for gateways that serve `host/bucket/key` rather than `bucket.host/key` — MinIO and SeaweedFS both want it. |
| `AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION` | the SDK default (`WHEN_SUPPORTED`) | Read by the AWS SDK, not by this product. Set it to `WHEN_REQUIRED` so a browser presigned PUT (which sends no checksum header) is accepted by S3-compatible gateways. |
| `AWS_RESPONSE_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION` | the SDK default | The reading half of the setting above; `WHEN_REQUIRED` for the same gateways. |

## Email

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SMTP_HOST` | unset (email is off) | SMTP host. With it unset the product never sends mail — invitations are copy-a-link instead, which is a workable self-host mode rather than a broken one. |
| `SMTP_PORT` | 587 | SMTP port. |
| `SMTP_SECURE` | false | Set to `true` for implicit TLS (port 465). STARTTLS on 587 is the `false` case. |
| `SMTP_USER` | unset (no authentication) | SMTP username. |
| `SMTP_PASS` | unset (no authentication) | SMTP password. |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | `<product name> <noreply@wikistead.local>` | From address on outgoing mail. Set it to a domain you actually control, or your mail will be filed as spam. |
| `EMAIL_OUTBOX_POLL_MS` | 5000 | How often the mail drain looks for queued messages. |
| `EMAIL_FOLD_WINDOW_S` | 30 | Hold window for immediate notifications: mentions arriving inside it fold into one message instead of a burst. |
| `EMAIL_DIGEST_HOUR` | 8 | Hour of day the daily digest is sent, in EMAIL_DIGEST_TZ. |
| `EMAIL_DIGEST_TZ` | UTC | Time zone the digest hour is interpreted in. |
| `UNSUB_TOKEN_TTL_S` | 2592000 (30 days) | How long an unsubscribe link in a notification email keeps working. |

## Sign-in

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OIDC_SECRET_ENC_KEY` | unset (required) | Base64 AES-256 key that encrypts tenant OIDC client secrets at rest. The server refuses to start without it rather than storing those secrets in plaintext, and refuses to start on the key published in the public repository's fixtures. |
| `OIDC_ISSUER` | unset | Issuer the collaboration server validates member tokens against. Per-workspace OIDC is configured in the product; this is the deployment-wide one collab checks. |
| `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | unset | Client id the development seed writes into the dev workspace's OIDC connection. Production workspaces register their own in the admin console, so this is a seeding convenience rather than a deployment setting. |
| `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | unset (a public client) | Client secret for the seeded development connection. It is encrypted with OIDC_SECRET_ENC_KEY before it reaches the database, exactly as a secret entered in the console would be. |
| `OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | unset | Redirect URI for the seeded development connection. It has to match what the identity provider has registered, including port. |
| `OIDC_JWKS_URI` | unset | JWKS endpoint matching OIDC_ISSUER. |
| `OIDC_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ISSUER` | off | Set to `1` to let a workspace register an OIDC issuer on a private network address. Off by default because it is the request a server-side request forgery needs. |
| `LOGIN_METHODS` | unset (every method permitted) | Comma-separated ceiling of sign-in methods this deployment allows (`tenant-oidc`, `platform-oidc`, `saml`). Workspaces choose within it; a value naming no valid method fails at boot rather than 404-ing every login. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_ISSUER` | unset (platform sign-in is off) | Issuer for the deployment-wide identity provider, used when a workspace has not registered its own. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | unset | Client id at the platform issuer. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | unset (public client) | Client secret at the platform issuer, when it issues one. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | unset | Redirect URI registered with the platform issuer. It must match exactly, including scheme and port. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_SCOPES` | openid email profile | Scopes requested from the platform issuer. |
| `PLATFORM_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` | groups | Claim carrying group membership, for deployments whose provider names it something else. |
| `LOCAL_LOGIN_WINDOW_S` | 900 | Window over which failed password attempts are counted. |
| `LOCAL_LOGIN_ID_MAX` | 5 | Failed attempts per account inside the window before it is locked. |
| `LOCAL_LOGIN_IP_MAX` | 30 | Failed attempts per source address inside the window, which is what bounds spraying across many accounts. |
| `LOCAL_LOGIN_LOCK_S` | 1800 | How long a lockout lasts. |
| `LOCAL_RESET_ADDR_MAX` | 3 | Password-reset requests accepted per address per window. |

## Second factors

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FACTOR_VERIFY_WINDOW_S` | 900 | Window over which failed second-factor attempts are counted. |
| `FACTOR_VERIFY_MAX` | 5 | Failed second-factor attempts inside the window before the door locks. |
| `FACTOR_VERIFY_LOCK_S` | 1800 | How long that lock lasts. |
| `MAX_FACTORS_PER_MEMBER` | 10 | How many factors one member may register. It bounds the enrolment surface rather than expressing a security policy. |
| `SECOND_FACTOR_RECOVERY` | on | Set to `off` to stop issuing recovery codes. Off means a member who loses every factor needs an administrator, which is the trade a deployment makes deliberately. |

## Guests and sharing

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GUEST_TOKEN_SECRET` | unset (required) | Signs the short-lived tokens anonymous share-link visitors carry. Production refuses to start on the value published in the public repository's fixtures. |
| `GUEST_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | 3600 | How long a guest token lives. Keep it short: after a link is revoked an already-connected guest keeps access until their token expires, and this is the length of that window. |
| `EXCHANGE_RL_IP_MAX` | 30 | Share-link token exchanges accepted per source address per minute. |
| `EXCHANGE_RL_LINK_MAX` | 10 | Token exchanges accepted per share link per minute, which bounds one leaked link rather than one visitor. |
| `SHARE_LINK_SWEEP_POLL_MS` | 60000 | How often expired share links are swept out of the authorization store. |

| Variable | Default | What it does |

| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | unset | Signing secret for the Stripe webhook, without which subscription changes are ignored. |

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SEARCH_OUTBOX_POLL_MS` | 2000 | How often the search index drain runs. It is the delay between an edit and the edit being findable. |
| `WEBHOOK_OUTBOX_POLL_MS` | 5000 | How often queued webhook deliveries are drained. |
| `TRASH_SWEEP_POLL_MS` | 3600000 (1 hour) | How often trashed pages past their retention are purged. |
| `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_RECHECK_MS` | 21600000 (6 hours) | How often verified custom domains are re-checked for ownership. Set to `0` to switch the sweep off while developing against a placeholder domain. |
| `ABUSE_FLAG_WINDOW_S` | 600 | Window over which repeated abuse reports from one source are folded into one flag. |
| `YDOC_STORE_BACKOFF_MS` | 500 | Base backoff for retrying a failed document persist in the collaboration server. |

## Diagrams

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PLANTUML_RENDER_URL` | unset (diagrams degrade to their source) | Kroki-compatible endpoint for rendering PlantUML. Setting it sends diagram SOURCE to that service, so a shared endpoint means user content leaves your deployment; self-host Kroki if that matters. ## Development and tooling

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SEED_TENANT_PLAN` | unset (the schema default) | Plan the seed puts on the development workspace, for working on a screen that only appears above a certain tier. |
| `DEV_CUSTOM_DOMAIN` | unset | Custom domain the seed mirrors onto the development workspace on every run, so it survives a `down -v`. Seeded as verified locally; production still requires the DNS challenge. |
| `DEV_ENROLL_POLICY` | the schema default (invite_only) | Enrolment policy the seed sets on the development workspace: `open`, `domain`, `groups` or `invite_only`. |
| `DEV_ENROLL_DOMAIN` | unset | Verified email domain for the seeded `domain` enrolment policy. |
| `DEV_ENROLL_ALLOWED_GROUPS` | unset | Comma-separated groups for the seeded `groups` enrolment policy. |
| `API_PROXY_TARGET` | http://localhost:4000 | Where the web dev server proxies `/api`. Development only — a built deployment reaches the API through its own origin. |
| `COLLAB_PROXY_TARGET` | http://localhost:4100 | Where the web dev server proxies the collaboration socket. |
| `VITE_TENANT` | unset | Workspace slug the dev web app pretends to be on, for working on a tenant other than the host name would resolve to. |
| `VITE_DEV_TOKEN` | unset | Bearer the dev web app sends instead of signing in. It only works against a server that is not in production mode. |
| `VITE_DEV_TOKEN_DISABLE` | unset | Set to turn the dev bearer off and exercise the real cookie session locally — the mode most sign-in bugs only appear in. |
| `WIKISTEAD_OPERATOR` | the OS user name | Name recorded as the actor when an operator CLI writes to the audit ledger. |
| `WKS_STACK_OFFSET` | 0 | Shifts every port and container name of the test stacks, so parallel checkouts can run their suites without colliding. |

## Not for operators

These exist so the product and its test harness can talk to themselves. Each one turns a guard off; setting one in a deployment is a way to break something quietly.

| Variable | Why it is here |
| --- | --- |
| `WIKISTEAD_SKIP_FGA_MODEL_GUARD` | Test harnesses set this to bring a server up against a store whose model is deliberately mismatched. A deployment that sets it turns off the check that its authorization model is the one it thinks it is. |
| `WIKISTEAD_TEST_STACK` | The test runner sets this to prove a suite is pointed at the isolated stack rather than a development database. Setting it by hand tells that guard a lie. |
| `POOL_END_QUIESCE_MS` | How long a shutdown waits for tenant connections that are on their way back before it forces the close (#773). It exists so a machine slow enough to miss the default can be given room; a deployment has no shutdown path to tune, and setting it high enough to matter would trade a reported hang for a silent one. |

## What this list cannot see

The walk reads `process.env.NAME` and the handed-in `env.NAME` form. A read through a computed key is invisible to it — `OIDC_SECRET_ENC_KEY` is fetched that way — so those rows are declared, and the check requires the name to keep appearing in the code (or in the file the row names) rather than trusting the declaration forever.

Enterprise Edition variables are not here: they are emitted by a generator inside that package, because a Community Edition tree does not contain it.
